newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firm targets higher Rolls-Royce sales in '96.
newsitem.headline: Japan firm targets higher Rolls-Royce sales in '96.

text.p: Cornes & Co Ltd, the sole importer and distributor for Rolls-Royce cars in Japan, said on Wednesday that it hopes to sell a total of 150 Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars in calendar 1996, up from 121 a year earlier.

Takao Watanabe, a director at Cornes, made the forecast during a news conference where the company launched the 1997 models of the Rolls-Royce and Bentley, both of which are made by Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Ltd.

Rolls-Royce Motor Cars is owned by Vickers Plc. Keith Sanders, a director of Rolls Royce Motor Cars, said business was progressing well with worldwide sales up over 25 percent in the first eight months of this year.
But he added: "We expect over 10 percent growth in worldwide sales this year."
Sanders said Rolls Royce sold 1,556 cars worldwide in 1995, up 10 percent from a year earlier.

The Japanese sales prices of most new models were unchanged from previous models despite improvements in several devices and an increase in engine power, Watanabe said. But the price of two-door models like the Bentley Continental was three to four percent higher than previous models, partly due to the weaker yen against the sterling, he said.
